title: First order thickenings of algebraic spaces and their ring sheaves
statement: Use algebraic spaces over a scheme $S$ and their small etale sites and structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A first order thickening $Z\hookrightarrow Z\prime$ means a representable closed immersion whose ideal sheaf has square zero and whose underlying closed subset is all of $Z\prime$; closed immersion is tested after every scheme base change, closed immersions of schemes being [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Module sheaves and quasi-coherence are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. If $Z\hookrightarrow Z\prime$ is a first order thickening, restriction gives an equivalence $Z\prime_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq Z_{\mathrm{et}}$. On this common site its ring sheaf is an extension $0\to\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_{Z\prime}\to\mathcal O_Z\to0$ with square-zero quasi-coherent kernel $\mathcal J$. Conversely, let $f:Z\to C$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$, and let $0\to\mathcal J\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal O_Z\to0$ be an exact sequence on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$, where $\mathcal A$ is a sheaf of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_C$-algebras, the last arrow is an algebra homomorphism, and $\mathcal J$ is a square-zero ideal quasi-coherent over $\mathcal O_Z$. There is a first order thickening $Z\hookrightarrow Z\prime$ over $C$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{Z\prime}\cong\mathcal A$ respecting the quotient and the $f^{-1}\mathcal O_C$-algebra structure. For two such thickenings over $C$ of the same $Z$, every homomorphism of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_C$-algebras between their ring sheaves on the common site $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ inducing the identity on $\mathcal O_Z$ comes from a unique morphism of thickenings over $C$, in the opposite direction, restricting to the identity on $Z$.

proof.text: Write $i:Z\hookrightarrow Z\prime$. The site-identification assertion of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-ringed-realization] applies to this first-order thickening; use its pullback equivalence to regard all ring and module sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules], $\mathcal O_{Z\prime}\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is surjective with quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J$ on $Z\prime$. Thus its kernel sequence is exact. The first-order hypothesis says $\mathcal J^2=0$. Apply the essential-image assertion of the same module lemma to $\mathcal F=\mathcal J$: its annihilation hypothesis is exactly $\mathcal J\mathcal J=0$. It gives a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module whose direct image is $\mathcal J$. Under the site equivalence this is the same ideal sheaf, with the quotient scalar action. Explicitly, two lifts of a local section of $\mathcal O_Z$ differ by a section of $\mathcal J$, whose product with $\mathcal J$ is zero; the quotient action is therefore well-defined. This proves every assertion in the forward direction.

source.place: Section-thickenings, fundamental equivalence; Tags 05ZS and 05ZT; forward ideal description using spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03MB and 04CJ(3).

proof.text: For the converse apply the realization assertion of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-ringed-realization] with $X=Z$, $B=C$, and $\mathcal G=\mathcal J$. The given quotient endows the ideal with exactly the $\mathcal O_Z$-action required there: lift a quotient section locally and multiply in $\mathcal A$, independently of its lift since $\mathcal J^2=0$. The hypotheses supply quasi-coherence, square-zero multiplication, and the $f^{-1}\mathcal O_C$-algebra quotient; the algebras here are commutative, as in the source 05ZT (rings and algebras are commutative throughout the Stacks Project), which is the commutativity of $\mathcal A$ that the realization assertion requires. The resulting $Z\hookrightarrow Z\prime$ is a first-order thickening over $C$, and the supplied ring-sheaf isomorphism respects the quotient, kernel inclusion, and base algebra structure, as required.

source.place: Tag 05ZT (lemma-first-order-thickening), with the already existing general realization node.

proof.text: For the final assertion label the thickenings $Z\hookrightarrow Z_1\prime$ and $Z\hookrightarrow Z_2\prime$ and let $\alpha:\mathcal O_{Z_2\prime}\to\mathcal O_{Z_1\prime}$ be the given base-algebra map. Apply the morphism assertion of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-ringed-realization] with both closed spaces equal to $Z$, $g=\mathrm{id}_Z$, and $B=C$. The reduction condition in that assertion is precisely that $\alpha$ induces the identity on $\mathcal O_Z$. It yields a unique $C$-morphism $Z_1\prime\to Z_2\prime$ inducing $\alpha$ and restricting to $\mathrm{id}_Z$. The order of the two labels gives the required opposite direction.

source.place: Tag 05ZN (lemma-first-order-thickening-maps), specialized to g = identity of Z.

lean.statement: theorem space_first_order_ringed_description {S : Scheme.{u}} : (∀ (X X' B : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ B) (i : X ⟶ X') (q : X' ⟶ B), IsSpaceFirstOrderThickening i → i ≫ q = f → ∃ (T : ThickeningOverModel f i q) (G : X.QCoh) (A : SpaceSquareZeroExtension f G.obj) (γ : T.toThickeningSiteModel.rings ≅ A.algebra.obj), γ.hom ≫ A.quotient = T.quotient ∧ ∀ (U : X.EtaleSite) (V : B.EtaleSite) (a : U.obj.left ⟶ V.obj.left) (ha : U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom.hom = yoneda.map a ≫ V.obj.hom), T.base.app U V a ha ≫ γ.hom.app (op U) = A.base.app U V a ha) ∧ (∀ (X B : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ B) (G : X.QCoh) (A : SpaceSquareZeroExtension f G.obj), ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpace S) (i : X ⟶ X') (q : X' ⟶ B), IsSpaceFirstOrderThickening i ∧ i ≫ q = f ∧ ∃ (T : ThickeningOverModel f i q) (γ : T.toThickeningSiteModel.rings ≅ A.algebra.obj), γ.hom ≫ A.quotient = T.quotient ∧ ∀ (U : X.EtaleSite) (V : B.EtaleSite) (a : U.obj.left ⟶ V.obj.left) (ha : U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom.hom = yoneda.map a ≫ V.obj.hom), T.base.app U V a ha ≫ γ.hom.app (op U) = A.base.app U V a ha) ∧ (∀ (X X' Y' B : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ B) (i : X ⟶ X') (j : X ⟶ Y') (q : X' ⟶ B) (r : Y' ⟶ B), IsSpaceFirstOrderThickening i → IsSpaceFirstOrderThickening j → i ≫ q = f → j ≫ r = f → ∀ (T : ThickeningOverModel f i q) (W : ThickeningOverModel f j r) (α : W.toThickeningSiteModel.rings ⟶ T.toThickeningSiteModel.rings), α ≫ T.quotient = W.quotient → (∀ (U : X.EtaleSite) (V : B.EtaleSite) (a : U.obj.left ⟶ V.obj.left) (ha : U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom.hom = yoneda.map a ≫ V.obj.hom), W.base.app U V a ha ≫ α.app (op U) = T.base.app U V a ha) → ∃! g' : X' ⟶ Y', i ≫ g' = j ∧ g' ≫ r = q ∧ ∀ U : X.EtaleSite, ∃ a' : (T.equivalence.inverse.obj U).obj.left ⟶ (W.equivalence.inverse.obj U).obj.left, T.reduction.app U ≫ a' = W.reduction.app U ∧ (T.equivalence.inverse.obj U).obj.hom ≫ g'.hom.hom = yoneda.map a' ≫ (W.equivalence.inverse.obj U).obj.hom ∧ (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat).map (Scheme.Γ.map a'.left.op) = α.app (op U))
